trust_decision.summary: DecayingModelController::import() decides which row an imported model writes to, which org owns it and whether it is a default model, by unsetting id/uuid and pinning org_id/default on the top level of the caller-supplied JSON before saving it flat.

landing_point.why: The summary names decaying model import; import() is the only import action and holds the strip-and-pin lines the fix replaces.

fix_sites.entry_point: POST /decayingModel/import (multipart DecayingModel[json] / submittedjson; ACL perm_admin or perm_decaying, app/Controller/Component/ACLComponent.php:222)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Nothing to dismiss: add(), edit(), enable/disable and massToggle already pin or fetch server-side, and the generic AppModel::save guard already rejects a flat record that also carries a nested alias key.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Importing a legitimate exported model (export() strips id/uuid/org_id) with name, parameters, formula, ref, version, enabled, all_orgs and attribute_types must still create a model and reset its attribute-type mappings.

O6_input_shapes: flat JSON object with top-level id/uuid/org_id/default
flat JSON object that also carries a nested DecayingModel alias key holding id/org_id/default
unknown/extra top-level keys dropped by the allow-list

O8b_injection_room.sibling: add() could take a non-wrapped REST body and strip id/org_id/default only at the top level, as import() did
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: add() already wraps a flat body at :212-214 and does the same unset/pin pattern at :216-219; a maintainer writing a REST-first variant could easily pin on the wrong level.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a bulk mapping import that takes model_id from the payload instead of the URL
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: resetMappingForModel() trusts $new_model['model_id'] (app/Model/DecayingModelMapping.php:30-47) and does no ownership check itself; only the controller guard at :33 protects it.

O9_family: mass assignment / authorization bypass on save (CWE-915, CWE-285)

O10_build.toolchain: CakePHP 2.x app (composer), Python PyMISP for tests/testregressions.py
O10_build.project_tests: tests/testregressions.py (PyMISP live-instance regression tests; the fix adds DecayingModelImportOwnership); no PHPUnit test found for DecayingModel

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Also unset $json['DecayingModel']['id'|'org_id'|'default'] next to the existing unsets, instead of building the row from an allow-list.

out_of_scope_notes: DecayingModelController::enable()/disable() REST error branches use `$array(...)` (a variable call) at app/Controller/DecayingModelController.php:466 and :514; a bug, not a security issue.
unverified: Likely already mitigated at the pinned commit: AppModel::save (app/Model/AppModel.php:160-183) returns false whenever data carries a non-empty nested alias array next to any top-level scalar. import() always sets scalar default/org_id (app/Controller/DecayingModelController.php:54-55), so the advisory's nested-alias payload seems to be refused before the fix. If so, the fix diff's regression test (fix.diff:108-135) would pass on the pinned tree and could not tell a solver's fix from no fix. This comes from reading CakePHP 2 Model::set semantics; I did not run it.
Whether CakePHP Model::save with $this->DecayingModel->id left over from earlier calls in one request could retarget the import save was not checked; the fix adds create() (fix.diff:41).
